title: Two-for-one has a boundary
hook: A promotion can change its effective price when you need an odd quantity.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Account for indivisible promotional bundles and odd demand.

misconception: Two-for-one always halves the checkout cost for the exact quantity needed.
objective: Account for indivisible promotional bundles and odd demand.

claims.text: Singles cost €3 each. A two-for-one pair costs €4; pairs are indivisible. Scaled model; fictional offer; pair-only purchase.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Items=3, A=€9 and B=€8. The geometry pictures follow the declared dimension relationships; other stage pictures are scaled to the larger displayed comparison and icons are not literal item counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",3,"x"]; B=["*",4,["ceil",["/","x",2]]]; x denotes Items. At x=3, A=9, B=8; recall at x=6: B=12. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals.

claims.text: A pair-only offer bills complete pairs. The ceiling rounds an odd requirement up, so the unneeded extra item still appears on the checkout total.

recall.question: Singles cost €3 each. A two-for-one pair costs €4; pairs are indivisible. Change only Items to 6. What is B (Pairs) now?
recall.why: Use B's stated rule with Items=6: it gives €12. A pair-only offer bills complete pairs. The ceiling rounds an odd requirement up, so the unneeded extra item still appears on the checkout total.
